candidate_windows.window_text:
Dependencies. We build and run our system with Pytorch 1.9.0 and AllenNLP 0.9.0 framework. We collect all verbs from the sentences in all datasets through spaCy<sup>10</sup> POS tagger. In addition, we obtain the constituency annotations through Stanford CoreNLP<sup>11</sup> and the dependency annotations through spaCy. We have total 27 types of constituency labels and 45 types of dependency labels.

Verb-tuple Alignment. We assume that every tuple has a verb in its relation (see Section 4). However, this assumption does not mean that each verb in a sentence can lead to one tuple. If a sentence contains multiple verbs identified by the POS tagger, we create multiple training instances. In each training instance, one verb is considered as the relation indicator, i.e., its $W_{verb}$ initialized to 1, while $W_{verb}$ for all other verbs in the sentence are initialized to 0. The corresponding tuple taking this verb as relation is the gold label for this training instance. If this verb does not lead to a tuple, we set the label for all words in the sentence to be "O", i.e., no tuple extracted for this verb. As such, the model is able to learn which verb leads to a tuple extraction. During testing, multiple test instances are created if a sentence contains multiple verbs; one verb serves as a relation indicator in each test instance. No tuple is extracted if all predictions of this test instance are "O".

Parameters. The hidden dimension $d_h$ for BERT representation $h_i^{bert}$ , Dep-GCN graph representation $h_i^{dep}$ , and Const-GCN graph representation $h_i^{con}$ is 768. We use single-layer GCNs for both constituency and dependency graphs. The hidden dimension $d_l$ for Dep-Encoder type embedding $l_i^{dep}$ and Const-Encoder path embedding $l_i^{con}$ is 400. Hyper-parameters $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are set to 0.024, 0.012, and 0.012, respectively. Hyper-parameters selection is based on grid searching. The experiments are conducted with Tesla V100 32GB GPU and Intel® Xeon® Gold 6148 2.40 GHz CPU.

Note that all baselines are implemented to extract $n$ -ary tuples on LSOIE-wiki and LSOIE-sci datasets, and binary tuples on CaRB dataset. 'CopyAttention', 'IMoJIE', and 'CIGL-OIE + IGL-CA' are binary OpenIE systems and cannot be tested naturally on LSOIE-wiki and LSOIE-sci datasets. We re-implement their models to cater $n$ -ary tuple extraction based on the code repositories. $^{12}$ In the evaluation, we evaluate 'CopyAttention', 'IMoJIE', and 'CIGL-OIE + IGL-CA' on LSOIE-wiki and LSOIESci datasets through our $n$ -ary re-implementations.
